import numpy as np
from scipy import stats
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression
from sklearn.feature_selection import mutual_info_classif
from collections import defaultdict

MAX_DRIVERS = 5

def design(feats):
    # Check if any feature shows significant association with outcome
    # using Welch's t-test and logistic regression
    p_threshold = 0.1
    corr_threshold = 0.6
    
    # Get all feature ids
    ids = feats.ids
    x = feats.x
    y = feats.y
    
    # Build correlation matrix to identify near-duplicates
    corr_matrix = np.corrcoef(x.T)
    
    # Identify near-duplicates (correlation >= 0.6)
    near_duplicates = set()
    for i in range(len(ids)):
        for j in range(i+1, len(ids)):
            if abs(corr_matrix[i,j]) >= corr_threshold:
                # Keep only one of the pair
                near_duplicates.add((ids[i], ids[j]))
    
    # Remove near-duplicates from consideration
    unique_ids = []
    seen = set()
    for fid in ids:
        if fid not in seen:
            unique_ids.append(fid)
            # Mark related features as seen
            for dup_pair in near_duplicates:
                if fid in dup_pair:
                    other_fid = dup_pair[0] if dup_pair[1] == fid else dup_pair[1]
                    seen.add(other_fid)
    
    # Compute Welch's t-statistics for each feature
    t_stats = []
    p_values = []
    for i, fid in enumerate(unique_ids):
        col_idx = feats.column(fid)
        group0 = x[y==0, col_idx]
        group1 = x[y==1, col_idx]
        if len(group0) > 0 and len(group1) > 0:
            t_stat, p_val = stats.ttest_ind(group0, group1, equal_var=False)
            t_stats.append(abs(t_stat))
            p_values.append(p_val)
        else:
            t_stats.append(0)
            p_values.append(1)
    
    # Find features with significant p-values
    significant_features = [fid for i, fid in enumerate(unique_ids) 
                           if p_values[i] < p_threshold]
    
    # If no significant features, return empty design
    if not significant_features:
        return Design(drivers=(), columns=(), products=(), loadings={})
    
    # For each significant feature, check if it's associated with outcome
    # across strata
    strata = feats.stratum
    strata_names = list(set(strata))
    
    # If we have more than one stratum, check for consistent effect
    if len(strata_names) > 1:
        # Simple approach: if effect is consistent across strata, include it
        pass  # For simplicity, we'll proceed with the significant features
        
    # Select top features based on t-statistic
    sorted_indices = np.argsort(t_stats)[::-1][:MAX_DRIVERS]
    selected_features = [unique_ids[i] for i in sorted_indices if i < len(unique_ids)]
    
    # Check if any feature shows strong enough effect to be considered a driver
    # We require at least one feature with p-value < 0.05
    strong_features = [fid for i, fid in enumerate(unique_ids) if p_values[i] < 0.05]
    
    # If no strong evidence, return empty design
    if not strong_features:
        return Design(drivers=(), columns=(), products=(), loadings={})
    
    # Otherwise, select top features based on significance
    # Use the first few significant features as drivers
    drivers = tuple(selected_features[:MAX_DRIVERS])
    
    # All features with p-values < 0.1 should enter the model
    columns = tuple([fid for i, fid in enumerate(unique_ids) if p_values[i] < 0.1])
    
    # No interaction terms in this simple version
    products = ()
    
    # Create loadings for weighted score
    loadings = {}
    for i, fid in enumerate(unique_ids):
        if p_values[i] < 0.1:
            loadings[fid] = t_stats[i]  # Weight by t-statistic
    
    return Design(drivers=drivers, columns=columns, products=products, loadings=loadings)
